title: Portal Line
summary: Lead travellers through a portal: fence the domain to make f one-one, fence the doors to make f onto, and count the one-one maps.
subject: mathematics
concepts: One-one and onto on a finite set
learningOutcome: The student can find where a function is one-one, find the co-domain that makes it onto, and count the one-one maps of a finite set onto itself.

levels.title: No shared doors
levels.adds: Baseline: f is one-one on an interval only if no two inputs share an output, so the fences stop at the turning points (Ex 1.2 Q1 to Q6, Q11).
hints: Two different travellers sharing a door means f is not one-one there.
Find where f turns: a parabola turns at its vertex, |x − c| at c.
Stop the fence at the turning point on Pip’s side, and go as far as you can the other way.

levels.title: Every door in use
levels.adds: New: onto means the co-domain equals the range; find the range of f on a stretch (Ex 1.2 Q5, Q7 to Q10; Examples 9 to 12).
hints: The doors in use are the values f takes on the stretch.
The largest and smallest are at the ends of the stretch or at a turning point inside it.
Put the fences exactly at the smallest and largest value.

levels.title: Counting the ways
levels.adds: New: for n travellers and n doors a one-one map is also onto, and there are n! of them (Misc Q4; Examples 13, 14, 22).
hints: The first traveller has n doors to choose from.
Each next traveller has one fewer door left.

misconceptions: x² is one-one on every interval
A function is onto whatever its co-domain is
On a finite set a one-one map need not be onto
